subject: Clarify micro-flooring, heartbeat prefix credits and invoice line mapping
body:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@luminaretail.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on micro-flooring / heartbeat prefix credits

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost breakdown were helpful. Procurement wants one clarifying item before we circulate the SOW: how exactly do you apply the ‘micro-floor’ to intermittent streaming calls and to heartbeat/prefix reuse? Two things in particular:

- If an end-user triggers a quick 6-token intent check (streaming) every 10 minutes, does each call incur the micro-floor, or is there any prefix/heartbeat aggregation that pools those into a single billable unit?
- For requests where we reuse the same prefix repeatedly (user history warmup), do we get prefix-crediting that reduces the billed tokens, or is the micro-floor applied after credits?

If you can point us to an example invoice line that maps these behaviors, that would be ideal — procurement wants a sample line item they can compare to their budget model. Attaching our internal template (billing_sample_lines.xlsx) for reference.

Best,
Susan
Senior Product Ops, LuminaRetail

Hi Susan — great questions. Short answer up front: micro-floor applies per-call by default, but our prefix-heartbeat crediting can effectively offset that for warm prefixes depending on reuse cadence. Details below and I attached a one-page sample invoice mapping to your template.

High level rules we used for your proposal (can be adjusted in Dedicated configs):
- Micro-floor: a minimum billing quantum applied per call (example: 32 token quantum). Applies to each discrete API request unless the request qualifies for session aggregation.
- Aggregation window: calls from the same client session within a 30-minute rolling window are grouped and billed as one aggregated session (your quick 6-token checks every 10 minutes would be grouped if they share session identifier).
- Prefix/heartbeat credit: when a prefix (e.g., conversation history) is reused across calls, we issue a prefix-credit that reduces billed tokens; credits are applied before micro-flooring. So if credits reduce the net billed tokens below the floor, the micro-floor still brings the final billed quantity up to the floor.

Example (mapped to your spreadsheet):
- 4 calls in 25 minutes, each nominally 6 tokens => raw billed tokens = 24.
- Prefix credits applied = 20 tokens (warm prefix reuse).
- Net tokens after credits = 4.
- Micro-floor = 32 => billed tokens = 32.

This is the conservative default (ensures predictable unit economics). We can configure alternate modes for Dedicated customers:
- 'Floor-after-aggregation' mode (grouping first, then floor) — default for most enterprise pilots.
- 'Floor-after-credits' vs 'Floor-before-credits' toggle (you asked specifically) — we support both; default is credits-first then floor.

I realize procurement will want a line-item that shows the steps. See attached sample invoice (Lumina_proposal_v2.pdf) and billing_sample_lines.xlsx filled with the example.

If that sounds acceptable I can loop in Karthik to map the final language to the SOW and to propose a concession if you want the alternative (floor-after-aggregation) behavior.

—Laura

Looping in to propose final sell language and a one-time pilot concession.

Hi team — quick proposal to close:
- Default billing behavior remains credits-first then micro-floor (as Laura outlined).
- For LuminaRetail pilot (3 months), offer a pilot concession: invoice-level safety-net that caps billed tokens for micro-floor-impacted flows to the higher of (actual net tokens after credits) or 50% of the micro-floor.
  - Example: micro-floor = 32 => pilot billed minimum = max(net_tokens_after_credits, 16).
- Rationale: gives Lumina a predictable downside while preserving our ability to enforce a minimum unit economics.

Ask: can Sergio sign off on the concession language and we include the clause in the SOW? I attached a redline to the proposal describing the concession language. If procurement agrees, we can ship the SOW + a sample invoice mapping.

Thanks,
